strengths: One road for an item that changes owner: a give, a loot, a rifle, a steal and a Plant all end in transferItem on a GM, which reads what moves and the hands it lands in off the GMs' marks after one wait for both sheets, chains both sheets in one sorted order, joins a piece to its stack by the carried identity, and rolls a copy back when the piece changed on the way (scripts/inventory.mjs:1136-1305).

One gate before anything is read: transferRefusal answers every mode's room, lives, phase and person before a Palm's rolls are read, so a refusal hands the action back on the Palm's browser and a refusal after the rolls keeps it spent, told as nothing carried out (scripts/inventory.mjs:1078-1106; scripts/palm.mjs:612-618, 699-706).

The planted item is a name, not a mark: every module item carries a random drpgItemId, preservedFlags carries it through every transfer, and which identity is poisoned lives only in the GMs' trapLedger; a used card's identity is held to its writer owning the character and still holding the item (scripts/inventory.mjs:30-49, 141-181; scripts/traps.mjs:443-446, 923-931, 1128-1159).

A trap disarms itself before its card, in the projects' queue, and a card that could not stamp is not sent; the card goes gmOnly so the killer's thread never learns who walked in (scripts/traps.mjs:280-373).

A stash's free reach is counted once a time of day in a GM store, stamped with no wait between read and write, taken off again when nothing moved, and a hidden stash's refusal reads like an empty one so a packet learns nothing of a hiding place (scripts/stash-reach.mjs:386-400, 452-537).
The owner of a rifled stash hears of it on walking in, once, never who or when, by two roads chained per owner so a paid crossing does not tell twice (scripts/stash-reach.mjs:570-653).
A use reads the item again after its windows, and a creative ruling is held one at a time per item on the GM and read again after the GM's window (scripts/use-items.mjs:555-568, 1003-1043).

Durability is worn on the roll that fills it and read off the GMs' copy where a GM's road holds one, so a mend a console wrote a moment before spares nothing (scripts/inventory.mjs:233-300; scripts/use-items.mjs:174-282).

The project-action use copy and the pass copy are sent addressed to their owner only, for their own characters only, taken only from a GM, and only grey a row: the GM's run stays the authority (scripts/facility-uses.mjs:1-14, 32-44, 95-108; scripts/lockpick-gm.mjs:22-28, 128-139, 188-201).

Everything a facility use is judged by is read on the GM: the room the GMs hold the character in, the action looked up in that room alone, the Overflow, the limit in one serial step per action key, and the roll off the GMs' record (scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:106-152; scripts/facilities-gm.mjs:38-52).

findings.title: A room action's Hope, Health and Sanity effects read the sheet as it stands, not as the GMs hold it: the E29 r2-H24 class reopened by E93
findings.where: scripts/facilities-gm.mjs:144-158 (applyEffects reads target.system.resources and writes with trustedWrite); scripts/sheet-audit.mjs:1000-1048 (meansWrite and the list of roads it covers); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:106-152 (handleFacilityUse: no judgedFor, no meansWrite before applyEffects)
findings.what_happens: applyEffects computes Health and Sanity from `target.system.resources[path].value`, and Hope from `r.hope.value` with the sheet's `r.hope.max`, then writes the result as a GM (`trustedWrite`, reason facility). sheet-audit.mjs's note on meansWrite records that a GM's write over a path supersedes a put-back pending on it, measured for seven roads that wrote Hope from a console's 5 for the GMs' 2 (E29 fix r2-H24), and that a Hope maximum is the world's less the scars, whatever the sheet says. Every road of that list now reads the GMs' marks through meansWrite (use-items.mjs `restore` among them); the E93 effects were written later and are not on the list and do not. handleFacilityUse waits on nothing of the student's queue before it applies the effects.
findings.failure_scenario: A player's console raises their own Hope from 2 to 5 and at once uses a project's room action that gives +1 Hope: the primary writes 6 as a GM's write before the put-back of 5 lands, and the student keeps 6 Hope where the GMs held 2.
findings.expected: The effects read and write the student's means as the GMs hold them, in one meansWrite job, as every other GM road that restores or spends a resource does since E29 fix r2-H24.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the health, sanity and hope branches of applyEffects in meansWrite(target, (held, maxOf) => ...), and add the road to meansWrite's list.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a wait or a held read on the facility road: handleFacilityUse calls gmPlaceOf, offerAt, overflowNow, the use store and spendAction (for a project's cost) and then applyEffects, with no judgedFor or itemAsHeld between; trustedWrite (resource-guard.mjs:350-354) only stamps the write and moves the GMs' mark to it (noteOwnWrite), which is the superseding the note describes. A GM's own action (the GM's roll on a GM's action) has the same read but no console behind it. Health and Sanity are flagged to the GMs rather than put back, so a console gains nothing there; Hope, put back at once, is the case that moves a number. Not run: no tier-2 test drives a facility Hope effect beside a pending put-back (git grep applyEffects over the tests finds E93-T5's timed trait only).
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 'E93-T5 - a room action's temporary +X to a trait ...' (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:100449) drives applyEffects for a timed trait only; tier 1 R6911 (scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:39008) reads applyEffects' source for giveBack. Results not read (no base-run.json).

findings.title: A Pick the Lock pass follows its holder by the room's name alone: a crossing on another scene into a room of the same name marks it used, and walking out there ends it
findings.where: scripts/lockpick-gm.mjs:70-81 (onPassCrossing); scripts/crossing-settle.mjs:55 (the event carries sceneId); scripts/movement.mjs:1210-1214 (holdsPass compares the scene)
findings.what_happens: A pass row holds `sceneId` and `room`, and holdsPass, the reader that lets the holder through, compares both. onPassCrossing, which marks the pass entered and ends it on the way out, compares only `event.to` and `event.from` with `row.room`, though the settled crossing hands it `sceneId`. A character with a token on a second scene that has a room of the same name - the case E12 wrote the scene rules for (traps.mjs:147-156, stash-reach.mjs:226-232) - marks the pass entered by walking into that other room, so it survives the time of day's end unused, and ends it by walking out of that other room before the lock was ever passed.
findings.failure_scenario: A student picks the school's Storage lock, then their token on the Annex walks into and out of the Annex's Storage: the pass is ended and the school's door they paid to open is shut to them again.
findings.expected: The pass's crossings are read on the pass's own scene, as holdsPass reads it.
findings.fix_sketch: In onPassCrossing, also require event.sceneId === row.sceneId (and leave an event with no sceneId to the room alone, as today).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked the event's shape (crossing-settle.mjs:55: sceneId present) and the other reader of the row (infiltrate-reroll.mjs:105-107, a Reroll, which compares the room alone too but only for the roller's own last pick). The tier-2 tests of onPassCrossing (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:102348-102371) pass no sceneId, so nothing pins either answer. The situation needs one character with tokens on two scenes and two rooms of one name; the module treats both as real (E12), so the case stands, rare.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 near scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:102348 (onPassCrossing with { actorId, from, to }, no scene). Result not read.

findings.title: A Plant of an item the planter no longer carries is answered as done: the planter reads 'In a moment you learn...' and nothing follows
findings.where: scripts/palm.mjs:795-835 (plantOnPerson's early `return null` and `return refuse(...)`, which answers null); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:649-664 (handlePlant passes on only `refused`); scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:1817-1820
findings.what_happens: plantOnPerson refuses with `{ refused }` for the one gate and an undecided item, but for an item that is no longer in the planter's pockets as the GMs hold them (`pool.find` misses) it calls `refuse(...)`, which logs and answers null; handlePlant then returns nothing and the runner answers the asker done. The planter's browser reads `res.ok` with no refusal and prints DRPG.Steal.plantSent ('In a moment you learn whether the item reached their pocket'), and no card follows because plantOnPerson returned before its whisper. The trust model's step 3 asks a run that did no work to answer 'nothing was carried out: ...'. stealFromPerson's two null answers (thief or victim gone, or the same sheet) are the same shape.
findings.failure_scenario: A player picks a kit to Plant, and while their two roll windows are open the GM takes the kit away (or a usable of it is spent): the Palm card says the result comes in a moment, the action stays paid, and no result ever comes.
findings.expected: '.claude/rules/trust-model.md', How to add a bridge action, step 3: a resolver that answers null for work it did not do is a refusal, 'nothing was carried out: ...', told as refused.
findings.fix_sketch: Answer { refused: "nothing was carried out: ..." } where plantOnPerson and stealFromPerson now answer null.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for an honest road that reaches line 834: palmablePool and pocketsFrom build the same pool (carried, no Truth Bullet, a known category), so only a change between the Palm window and the GM's read reaches it - a GM's Take, a theft by another student, a use of the last charge does not (a broken item stays in the pool). The bridge's guards (owns plannerId) keep a packet from naming someone else's item, so what remains is a timing and a hand-written packet.

findings.title: The key rule's branch answers a stuck removal as a clean move: ok, stuck false, and the GMs not told
findings.what_happens: Where the taker already holds a key to the room, transferItem copies nothing and takes the giver's key off with takeOne. takeOne answers `{ stuck: true, left: 1 }` when the delete did not land (a refused write resolves quietly) and `{ stuck: true, left: count }` when a count write did not; the branch only asks `"left" in taken`, so both answer `{ ok: true, ..., stuck: false }`, the taker is whispered that they still hold one key, and no GM card goes out. The function's own doc says `stuck` is true when the giver's piece could not be taken off and that the GMs are told either way; the main road below does both (1297-1301).
findings.failure_scenario: A thief who already holds a key to Room 3 lifts the stash's copy and the delete is refused on the GM: the thief reads 'You take Room 3 key out of Aiko's stash', Aiko's stash still holds it, and no GM is told.
findings.expected: As the main road: stuck true and the TRANSFER_STUCK line to the GMs when takeOne answers stuck.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a caller that reads `left` against the count to notice it: stealFromVault, stealFromPerson and the hand-over read ok, copy, keyHeld and stuck only. The trigger is a write a pre-hook refused, which the comment at 1180-1182 says resolves as quietly as one that landed, so it is possible but rare; practical harm is small, since the taker held a key already.

findings.title: Throwing a broken thing away does not read the item again after its two windows, as using one does since S08-35
findings.where: scripts/use-items.mjs:884-997 (discardBroken: checks at 893-902, then the confirm 906-916 and the roll 922-929, then the trace 938-951 and the delete 979-983); against 555-568 (useItem's read after its windows)
findings.what_happens: discardBroken asks broken and not stashed once, before the confirm and the Shadow roll, both of which wait on the player. useItem reads the item again after its windows because 'the item can go meanwhile - stolen, handed over, used up by a second click, put away' (S08-35); discardBroken does not. findings.refutation_tried: Looked for the GM refusing the trace for an item no longer held: handleRemnant files the type by its own reading (use-items.mjs:827-829, 939) but the trace is placed at the console's word with its band (trust model, layer two), and nothing on that road reads the item. findings.title: The trap listeners no longer start with the armed map: a crossing reads two GM stores first, and any actor write drops the map
findings.where: scripts/traps.mjs:33-39 (the header's rule), 938-964 (onCrossed: hasPendingStashNotice and hasPendingBedroomNote before armed()), 749-751 (updateActor drops the index), 986-992
findings.what_happens: The header says every listener 'starts with a lookup in armed() - a Map built once and rebuilt only when the projects change - and returns on a miss before touching an actor, a token or a setting'. Since 1.2.112 onCrossed first awaits the rifle store's hydration and scans its rows, then imports doors-gm.mjs and scans the bedroom notes, on every crossing the primary hears, before the map. And the map is dropped on every updateActor, so a paid crossing (an action spent is an actor write) makes the next event rebuild it from projectMeta and every countdown.
findings.failure_scenario: No player sees it; on the primary every crossing costs two store scans and, after any sheet write, a rebuild of the trap map - a cost the header says is not paid.
findings.expected: The header and the code to agree; a cost per crossing measured by scenario 86 (frame-work) if it matters.
findings.refutation_tried: Both stores are small (rows only while a notice waits) and the rebuild is linear in projects, so this is a comment that stopped being true more than a slowdown; not measured.
